metadata.title: Organic Shopping: feed quality to commercial learning
metadata.workstream: L — Organic Google Shopping / product feeds
metadata.scope: Reusable client-account audit informed by SEOasis public methodology. SEOasis itself is an agency; no merchant account was audited.
metadata.limitations: No Merchant Center, GA4, Shopify or product-feed account access. No client eligibility, feed quality, revenue, conversion or incremental-lift conclusion.

summary: SEOasis publicly connects feed ownership, product attributes and controlled listing improvements to revenue-oriented reporting. Start with eligibility and measurement, then test a viable product cohort.

findings.title: Feed optimization is already part of SEOasis’s public playbook
findings.evidence: The Bronson case describes feed rebuilding, required attributes, title/description enrichment and ongoing issue monitoring. This verifies published methodology, not completed client implementation.

source.title: Bronson Vitamins: Google Merchant Center Case Study | SEOasis | SEOasis
source.note: Saved public HTML describes Merchant Center feed ownership, attribute enrichment, title work, diagnostics and reporting. No private account or causal validation.

findings.businessImplication: A client operating board can use the agency’s existing language: feed quality → eligible products → qualified shopping visits → commercial outcomes.

findings.title: The founder describes supplemental feeds and title/image tests
findings.evidence: The attributable Productrise interview discusses supplemental-feed workflows and testing product presentation; vendor-hosted results were not independently audited.

source.title: Interview with Mike Sack on organic shopping - Productrise Blog
source.note: First-person founder Q&A hosted by a vendor; supplemental feeds and title/image experiments are attributable methodology. Outcomes are self-reported.

findings.businessImplication: Offer a bounded test framework with an owner, change log, comparable product cohort and stop/scale decision.

findings.title: Free listings serve product pages
findings.evidence: Google documents free listings as product-page discovery; collection-page strategy is a separate, complementary client workstream.

source.title: Free listings for products - Google Merchant Center Help
source.note: Free listings promote eligible product pages. Activation and eligibility do not guarantee appearance; shipping, return and policy checks remain necessary.

findings.businessImplication: Map feeds to product/variant destinations and collections to category intent. Keep separate metrics for each.

findings.title: Reported channel growth is a useful hypothesis, not an incrementality estimate
findings.evidence: The Bronson case compares channels and attributes an outcome to feed work. Without baseline exports, treatment/control design and trading context, the causal size of the contribution remains undetermined.

source.title: Bronson Vitamins: Google Merchant Center Case Study | SEOasis | SEOasis
source.note: Saved public HTML describes Merchant Center feed ownership, attribute enrichment, title work, diagnostics and reporting. No private account or causal validation.

findings.businessImplication: Ask for period definitions, channel setup, sample size, stock/promotion history and reconciled orders before forecasting.

findings.title: Account health and outcomes need private validation
findings.evidence: No client account, catalog export or order data was available to this public study.

source.title: View ad campaigns performance in Merchant Center - Google Merchant Center Help
source.note: Merchant Center Analytics can separate free listings and ads and segment product, brand and category. Different reporting surfaces can use different tracking definitions.

findings.metric: Eligible items, free-listing clicks, attributed orders and reconciled net sales
findings.whyItMatters: Distinguishes feed delivery, acquisition and commercial outcome.
findings.decision: Fix eligibility first, test presentation next, scale only after commercially useful evidence.

experiments.title: Pilot one title structure in a matched product cohort
experiments.evidence: Proposed experiment; no baseline, lift or target is assumed.

source.title: Interview with Mike Sack on organic shopping - Productrise Blog
source.note: First-person founder Q&A hosted by a vendor; supplemental feeds and title/image experiments are attributable methodology. Outcomes are self-reported.

experiments.hypothesis: A clearer product attribute order could improve qualified free-listing visits.
experiments.design: Choose comparable product cohorts using actual category, stock and prior performance; change titles only for the treatment group. Log promotions, price and other changes.
experiments.primaryMetric: Reconciled contribution or net sales per eligible product, subject to access and sufficient data
experiments.decision: Pre-register the observation window and minimum useful effect after baseline access. Scale, revise, continue collecting data or stop; do not force a significance claim.

experiments.title: Test images as a separate release
experiments.evidence: Proposed test reflects public founder commentary.

source.title: Interview with Mike Sack on organic shopping - Productrise Blog
source.note: First-person founder Q&A hosted by a vendor; supplemental feeds and title/image experiments are attributable methodology. Outcomes are self-reported.

experiments.design: Run after title testing or on a separate cohort. Check real product fidelity and current policies; keep source assets and rollback ready.
experiments.primaryMetric: Qualified shopping response and reconciled product outcomes
experiments.decision: Retain the variant only when evidence justifies it; distinguish low data volume from no effect.

releaseGates: Named owner and approved source-of-truth fields
Processed-item spot check after feed refresh
Product/variant destination, price and stock match
No new blocking issues in the reviewed cohort
Change log, reporting window and rollback recorded
